Gaming / Game craft

The worlds we hear before we see

Listen to how a game tells you where you are.

✳
The Offbeat EditCulture Issue · 1 min read

IN THIS STORY

Find the signalsListen between the actionRejoin the gameMore from Gaming

Find the signals

A game can use sound to mark distance, movement, or a change in danger. In a familiar area, notice what you hear before you turn the camera.

Keep the volume comfortable. Check the available subtitle, visual-cue, and audio settings so you can choose a presentation that works for you.

Listen between the action

Quiet spaces can have their own vocabulary: wind, machinery, a distant creature, or music that changes as you move. Try standing still somewhere safe and noticing the layers.

Treat your observations as impressions. Unless a developer has explained a system, you cannot know from a single moment exactly how the sound is triggered.

Rejoin the game

Return to normal play and notice whether the world feels easier to read. Paying attention once can make familiar spaces feel unexpectedly new.

If you share a clip, include the title and avoid spoilers. A small piece of sound design can be worth celebrating without revealing the whole scene.

“Listen to how a game tells you where you are.”
